episodes.156775: A high based squall line, exhibiting little to no lightning, roared southeast through north Alabama during the late afternoon and early evening. The initial gust front was likely responsible for the highest wind gusts and observed damage. Widespread measured wind gusts of 40-55 mph were observed. Estimated gusts of 60 mph likely occurred as well given the number of trees being knocked down in the area. However, no official wind measurements of 58 mph or higher were recorded.
episodes.156776: A high based squall line, exhibiting little to no lightning, roared southeast through southern middle Tennessee during the late afternoon and early evening.  The initial gust front was likely responsible for the highest wind gusts and observed damage. Widespread measured wind gusts of 40-55 mph were observed. Estimated gusts of 60 mph likely occurred as well given the number of trees being knocked down in the area.  However, no official wind measurements of 58 mph or higher were recorded.
episodes.157012: Numerous thunderstorms developed over the mainland and moved across the Brevard County intracoastal and nearshore coastal waters during the evening. A few of the storms produced strong/severe wind gusts near the coast before the storms moved to the Atlantic.
episodes.157041: Thunderstorms that moved offshore of the Space and Treasure Coasts in Central Florida produced several strong wind gusts.
episodes.157403: Clusters of thunderstorms organized into a more consolidated convective system over western Kentucky. The storms organized along and ahead of a cold front moving southeastward into southeast Missouri and adjacent southern Illinois. Cold mid-level temperatures and resulting steep lapse rates supported moderate instability, despite relatively modest low-level moisture. Strong unidirectional deep-layer wind flow resulted in fast storm motion and locally strong wind gusts as the storms crossed the Kentucky Lake region and Pennyrile region of west Kentucky.
episodes.157404: Clusters of thunderstorms strengthened along and ahead of a cold front moving southeastward into southeast Missouri. As daytime heating continued through the afternoon, the storms produced isolated hail up to nickel size. Cold mid-level temperatures and resulting steep lapse rates supported moderate instability, despite relatively modest low-level moisture.
episodes.157405: A small cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms moved south-southeastward ahead of a cold front crossing the Mississippi River. Diurnal heating resulted in steep low-level lapse rates in a narrow corridor ahead of the cold front across central and southern Illinois. Steep mid-level lapse rates existed atop these steep low-level lapse rates, resulting in at least 7.0 degree C/km lapse rates from the surface to above 500 mb. A few storms in this environment produced large hail. Additionally, increased surface vorticity existed in the immediate vicinity of the frontal boundary. The  combination of the steep lapse rates and surface vorticity resulted in a unique environment for brief landspouts. One such landspout occurred in the Interstate 64 corridor.
episodes.157406: Clusters of thunderstorms organized into a more consolidated convective system over southwest Indiana. The storms organized along and ahead of a cold front moving southeastward into southeast Missouri and adjacent southern Illinois. Cold mid-level temperatures and resulting steep lapse rates supported moderate instability, despite relatively modest low-level moisture. Strong unidirectional deep-layer wind flow resulted in fast storm motion and locally strong wind gusts as the storms crossed southwest Indiana.
episodes.157542: On Wednesday May 5th, an upper level disturbance moved southeast from southeast Colorado and southwest Kansas across the northeast combined Panhandles and western Oklahoma. This created thunderstorms that moved southeast across the eastern Oklahoma Panhandle and northeast Texas Panhandle. While instability appeared somewhat marginal for severe storms, one of the storms did become severe and produced quarter sized hail in Lipscomb County.
episodes.157579: A cold front triggered a broken line of strong to severe thunderstorms across south-central Illinois during the afternoon of May 6th.  Four brief tornado touchdowns occurred with the stronger cells, including one that did minor damage to a property just southwest of Assumption in Christian County.  Other thunderstorms dropped hail as large as quarters and produced minor wind damage.
episodes.157614: A passing upper level short wave trough over a moist and unstable airmass supported a few strong to severe storms that developed across NE FL south of a Gainesville to St Augustine line in the afternoon.
episodes.157735: An upper-level trough east of the MS Valley, with its base over FL, and an embedded shortwave moving across South FL helped a late season cold front push through the region. This in combination with both the Atlantic and Gulf sea breezes developing and interacting with one another along/near the I-95 corridor allowed for ample surface convergence to occur. Environmental parameters were favorable for the development of strong to severe storms, which produced small hail, flooding, and damaging winds across the east coast metro areas of South Florida.
episodes.157736: An upper-level trough east of the MS Valley, with its base over FL, and an embedded shortwave moving across South FL helped a late season cold front push through the region. This in combination with both the Atlantic and Gulf sea breezes developing and interacting with one another along/near the I-95 corridor allowed for ample surface convergence to occur. This activity then pushed eastward and offshore. Environmental parameters were favorable for the development of strong to severe storms, which produced hail and damaging winds across the Atlantic and Biscayne Bay waters of South Florida.
episodes.158420: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms moved across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours on May 6. Numerous reports of wind damage were received, and one person was killed and another injured in Robertson County.
episodes.158427: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a cold front during the evening of the 5th, with a couple large hail reports received in western OK.
episodes.158445: A line of showers and thunderstorms developed along an advancing cold front during the afternoon hours of May 6th. Initially, there were scattered reports of damaging wind and large hail across Northeast Arkansas and Northwest Tennessee. The wind threat increased as the line moved into southeast portions of West Tennessee and Northeast Mississippi where numerous reports of damage occurred.
episodes.158446: A line of showers and thunderstorms developed along an advancing cold front during the afternoon hours of May 6th. Initially, there were scattered reports of damaging wind and large hail across Northeast Arkansas and Northwest Tennessee. The wind threat increased as the line moved into southeast portions of West Tennessee and Northeast Mississippi where numerous reports of damage occurred.

episodes.158870: When the wind starts kicking up, there is probably something coming. Such was the case on the 9th, with south to southwest winds gusting from 30 to 40 mph in parts of Arkansas as of 500 am CST. At that time, a cold front was entering the northwest corner of the state from the Plains.||By 1200 pm CST, temperatures ahead of the front were in the mid 70s to lower 80s across the central/southern counties. Dewpoints were in the mid 60s to lower 70s (humid). These were favorable conditions for thunderstorm development, and a Severe Thunderstorm Watch was posted until 900 pm CDT. It felt like another season behind the front. Thermometers were showing readings in the mid 50s in parts of the Ozark Mountains including Bentonville and Rogers (both in Benton County). Winds had shifted to the north.||The first severe storm of the afternoon tracked from southern Van Buren County into Faulkner County. At 130 pm CST, quarter size hail occurred about six miles north of Enola (Faulkner County). Fifteen minutes later, golf ball to baseball size hail pelted the Mount Vernon (Faulkner County) community.||Between 230 pm and 600 pm CST, the focus shifted farther south. Golf ball size hail came down near Kimberley (Pike County), Chambersville (Calhoun County), and Thornton (Calhoun County). There were ping pong balls at Bearden (Ouachita County), and half dollars at Camden (Ouachita County). Thunderstorm gusts downed trees at   Hilo (Bradley County).
